mathematical_justification.clause: Boundary word, wraparound and all nonroot leaves
mathematical_justification.assessment: boundaryIndex g k is g+k+1 for every k:Fin n. Thus positions are exactly0 through n-1=N. The checked first/last theorems return P(g+1) and P(g), the latter using the actual equality n=0 in ZMod n. boundaryWord_leaf_edge identifies consecutive boundary vertex differences with the actual labelled edge g+k+1, for every0<=k<n-1. boundaryIndex_injective proves no two boundary positions give the same occurrence label. The independent leaf_index_exhaustion check proves every such leaf label differs from g and every e!=g occurs, by taking k=(e-g).val-1. Its positivity follows from e!=g and its bound from ZMod.val_lt; no leaf occurrence is omitted at the cyclic wraparound. These are occurrence statements and do not assume the physical tuple injective.

The checked boundaryWord_shift handles an arbitrary shift a with root g-a, hence the source generator g->g-1 is included. Algebraically the added a in shift cancels the subtracted root shift. The existing edge and edgeSegment shift lemmas and the independent tests preserve the same placed root and its orientation. Interval/composition data depend only on the unchanged finite order positions and therefore require no relabelling of those positions. The combinatorial definitions themselves need neither G1 nor G2; making them available on all tuples preserves their restriction to the source section domain. The independent distinct-boundary-vertices check uses only G1 to compose actual tuple injectivity with boundaryIndex_injective. G2 is never assumed.

BoundaryInterval is exactly a pair of positions left,right:Fin n together with left<right. This is the source integer domain0<=i<j<=N, presented by bounded natural positions. leaves is exactly right.val-left.val, not a separately supplied size. The positivity lemma derives its nonzeroness. Each part uses successive cuts k.castSucc and k.succ, and strict monotonicity proves it is a valid increasing interval. The independent cut_containment theorem derives every cut is between the fixed first and last cuts; it also derives every part has positive leaf count. No cut outside the original interval can enter the represented type.
